content: 1. A reactive self-test result should be followed by clear guidance on where and how to access additional support services. 2. In the Philippines, the smallest administrative division is referred to as a barangay, which is the native Filipino term for a village, district, or ward. 3. Over a five-month period, the LPCSC distributed 199 self-testing kits within Guangdong province, priced at approximately 23 USD, which included a refundable deposit of 16 USD upon submission of feedback. 4. Of the 199 users, 174 provided online feedback, and four individuals reported reactive HIV test results. 5. Six clients who used the self-testing service sought follow-up care on-site at LPCSC. 6. Unsupervised self-testing kits are available online, with prices ranging from 5 USD to 16 USD. 7. LPCSC operates China’s first and most widely recognized website for men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender individuals, serving as a platform for health education and surveys. 8. Annually, the LPCSC website receives over 500,000 unique visits and retains 100,000 registered members, as reported by Google Analytics. 9. At HIV testing service (HTS) sites, CDC staff provide on-site HIV confirmatory testing and collect relevant data. 10. LPCSC offers high-quality, timely preand post-test peer counseling, psychosocial support, and ensures retention in care, creating a one-stop, easily accessible HTS service. 11. Between January 2008 and December 2013, 22,282 MSM accessed HTS in Guangzhou through this program. 12. During this period, the annual number of MSM accessing HTS increased sevenfold, from 1,064 in 2008 to 7,754 in 2013. 13. The program successfully provided HTS to 80% of the estimated MSM population in Guangzhou and identified 82% of newly diagnosed HIV cases among MSM. 14. From 2008 to 2014, a total of 999 HIV-positive MSM cases were detected through this HTS program, accounting for 57% of all HIV-positive MSM cases in Guangzhou City. 15. Among these cases, 95% of clients were linked to the national HIV/AIDS care and support program, with 89% retained in care, receiving regular follow-up and biannual CD4 testing. 16. Founded in 2011, Love Yourself is a non-governmental organization based in Manila, primarily funded by the Research Institute for Tropical Medicine (RITM). 17. Love Yourself promotes self-acceptance among MSM and mobilizes them to access HTS services at the RITM satellite clinic, where all services are provided free of charge. 18. The clinic offers rapid HIV testing, preand post-test counseling, and additional testing for syphilis and hepatitis B, in accordance with national policy. 19. If two consecutive rapid HIV tests are reactive, clients are referred to the RITM hospital for clinical assessment and confirmatory testing. 20. Individuals diagnosed as HIV-positive are closely followed by volunteers and provided with treatment adherence counseling. 21. Love Yourself also offers a discreet third-party service, coordinating HIV testing at a private location convenient for the client, with same-day results and referrals. 22. Since 2011, nearly 200 clinic-based volunteers have been recruited as peer educators, all of whom are HIV-negative, promoting the message that it is possible to be sexually active and free of HIV. 23. The RITM Satellite Clinic in Malate serves 20 to 40 clients daily, primarily referred through online social media and networking campaigns. 24. Approximately 7% of clients tested at the clinic are diagnosed as HIV-positive, with 92% enrolled in antiretroviral treatment and care. 25. Adherence counseling provided by the clinic has resulted in an 85-90% success rate in retaining individuals on treatment. 26. In Vietnam, the decentralization of HTS from district primary healthcare to commune health stations (CHS) has improved access to testing services, though remote districts still face significant challenges. 27. To address this, the Vietnam Authority for HIV/AIDS Control and the Ministry of Health, with support from WHO and UNAIDS, piloted community-based HTS in high-burden provinces such as Thanh Hoa and Thai Nguyen. 28. The program offered bi-monthly HTS in select villages with high numbers of people who inject drugs, involving CHS staff, village health workers, and peer educators trained to provide rapid HIV testing. 29. Individuals with reactive test results had venous blood samples collected and sent to confirmatory laboratories, with confirmed HIV-positive clients linked to outpatient clinics for treatment and care. 30. The positivity rate in this pilot program was approximately four times higher than rates observed at health facilities in the same districts. 31. Five of the seven newly diagnosed HIV cases initiated antiretroviral therapy. 32. The pilot program demonstrated that community-based HTS is a feasible and effective method to increase awareness of HIV status among people who use drugs and their partners. 33. Peer educators and village health workers played a critical role in reaching the target population. 34. This model will inform Vietnam’s national AIDS program in developing further guidelines for community-based HTS. 35. Globally, innovative programs are being developed to address the needs of populations affected by HIV, tailoring services to meet specific community requirements. 36. These programs are overcoming social, legal, political, and logistical challenges by creating new ways to encourage service uptake. 37. The interventions highlighted in this compilation represent leaders in the field of HTS delivery, offering valuable insights for improving HIV testing globally.
